conventions.convention: The Gaussian construction and Fourier-uniqueness route assume the Axiom of Choice; Countable Choice is obtained from it where required.
Chi-square degrees are nonnegative integers, with chi-square zero defined as the point mass at zero.
Student t and Fisher F degrees are positive integers. Their ratio versions equal zero on denominator-zero sets, which have probability zero under the defining laws.
For u in (0,1), the quantile is the unique support point where the continuous, strictly increasing CDF equals u.
The normal sample has n ≥ 2 and positive variance; sample variance divides the residual squared sum by n−1.
Regression designs are deterministic and have full column rank, with n > p ≥ 1. Contrasts are nonzero. Nested-model F calibration assumes the mean belongs to the reduced space and 1 ≤ q ≤ p < n.

load_bearing.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let n ≥ 1, let Z ∼ N_n(0,I_n) have independent standard-normal coordinates, and let U satisfy UᵀU = I_n. Then UZ also has independent N(0,1) coordinates.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For Z ∼ N_n(0,I_n) and an orthogonal projection P of rank r, 0 ≤ r ≤ n, PZ and (I_n−P)Z are independent, their squared norms have laws chi-square r and chi-square n−r, and those squared norms are independent. Rank zero and full rank are included.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For every integer k ≥ 1, chi-square k has the displayed positive density on (0,∞), is positive almost surely, and has a CDF continuous on R and strictly increasing on (0,∞).

Under the Axiom of Choice and positive integer degrees, t_k is the law of G/√(Q_k/k) for independent standard normal G and chi-square Q_k; F_{r,s} is the law of (Q_r/r)/(Q_s/s) for independent chi-square variables. Each defining map equals zero when its denominator variable is zero.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Positive-degree t CDFs are continuous, strictly increasing on R, symmetric about zero, and have limits zero and one. Positive-degree F CDFs are continuous on R, zero on (−∞,0], strictly increasing on (0,∞), and tend to one. Each law has exactly one u-quantile on its support for every u ∈ (0,1).

Under AC, an independent normal sample with n ≥ 2 and σ > 0 has independent sample mean and sample variance, (n−1)S²/σ² ∼ chi-square n−1, S > 0 almost surely, and the displayed zero-extended studentized mean has law t_{n−1}. Its central quantile interval has exact coverage 1−α for every 0 < α < 1.

Under AC, deterministic full-column-rank X with n > p ≥ 1 and independent normal errors of positive variance gives independent least-squares coefficients and residual sum, RSS_X/σ² ∼ chi-square n−p, and exact t_{n−p} pivots for nonzero contrasts. For nested spaces of dimensions p−q and p, 1 ≤ q ≤ p < n, the displayed zero-extended residual-ratio statistic has law F_{q,n−p} under the reduced-space mean null, with independent chi-square contributions.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. For integer k ≥ 1, chi-square k is the law of the squared Euclidean norm of k independent standard normals; chi-square zero is the point mass at zero.

concerns.concern: The Statement writes f_k(x) = c_k x^{k/2−1} exp(−x/2) 1_{x>0}. Literally, the power factor is undefined at x = 0 for k = 1 and need not be real at negative x for odd k; multiplication by the zero indicator does not define it there. The proof establishes the intended density on positive x and zero elsewhere. An explicit piecewise zero extension would remove this pointwise notation issue.

alerts.finding: The published Statement begins 'Let f and (f_n) be measurable complex-valued functions' and later uses '∫ g dμ', but neither Statement nor Given binds an ambient measure space or introduces μ. This leaves the domain, measurability, and almost-everywhere convention implicit. Batch 10's applications supply the chi-square probability measure and integrable majorant 1, so their use is sound; the supplier should explicitly bind an arbitrary measure space (X,A,μ).

seams_checked.note: The normal-sample and regression theorems use def-statistic-and-estimator as a measurable data map on the explicitly stated Borel experiments. They establish measurability of the mean and least-squares maps and assume no parameter-space measurability or random-seed representation.

The page prose and ex-exact-unknown-variance-normal-t-interval preserve AC, n ≥ 2, positive variance, the t_{n−1} law, and continuous symmetric quantiles. Restricting to the common full-measure Borel set S > 0 makes its unextended quotient legitimate and preserves exact repeated-sampling coverage.

thm-wald-score-likelihood-ratio-asymptotic-chi-square F9 and step 4.1 use chi-square q as the squared norm of independent standard normals, with q ≥ 1 and AC, and retain asymptotic calibration. The opened normal-location examples correctly use chi-square one for a squared standard normal and chi-square zero for the boundary mixture atom.
